{{short description|German glass artist (born 1934)}}
'''Rosemarie Lierke''', born '''Rosemarie Lindner''' (December 1934 in [[Berlin]]), is a German glass artist, trained mathematician and a researcher into the history and technology of ancient glass production. Some of her artwork is held in the [[Museum Kunstpalast]] in [[Düsseldorf]], Germany.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014 |title=Geburtstag von Rosemarie Lierke (Rosemarie Lierke's birthday) |url=https://www.pressglas-korrespondenz.de/aktuelles/pdf/pk-2014-4w-ricke-lierke-geburtstag-2014.pdf |access-date=2025-10-28 |website=Der Glasfreund |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Katalog der Deutschen Nationalbibliothek |url=https://portal.dnb.de/opacPresentation?cqlMode=true&reset=true&referrerPosition=0&referrerResultId=idn=172238803&any&query=idn=11771514X |access-date=2025-10-28 |website=portal.dnb.de}}</ref>

== Biography ==
After graduating from high school in 1953 in Schnepfenthal, [[Thuringia]], Germany, Lierke studied mathematics in [[Berlin]] and [[Cologne]] from 1953 to 1960. From 1962 to 1967, she was a research assistant at the [[RWTH Aachen University|Technical University of Aachen]]. She also began to work with enameling, for which she built her own kiln for high-temperature tasks.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Rosemarie Lierke |url=http://rosemarie-lierke.de/index.html#expand |access-date=2025-10-28 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725043826/http://rosemarie-lierke.de/index.html#expand |archive-date=2024-07-25}}</ref>

In 1967, she moved to [[Toledo, Ohio]] in the United States with her husband, the physicist Ernst-Günter Lierke, and their two sons. At that time, Toledo called itself the "Glass Capital of the World." There she learned about the American [[studio glass]] movement and began making new artwork in glass, which she continued to do after she returned to Germany in 1970.<ref name=":1" /> 
[[File:Portland Vase BM Gem4036 n5.jpg|thumb|[[Portland Vase]]: example of cameo glass]]
From 1975 to 1979, Lierke worked as a mathematics teacher at the high school in Sulzbach (Taunus). From 1977 to 1987, she retreated to her glassblowing workshop in [[Schwalbach am Taunus]], investigating lamp-working techniques and inventing a new [[Craquelure|craquelé]] technique, which she [[patent]]ed in 1979.<ref name=":1" />

In 1987, she returned to the United States, this time going to [[Pasadena, California]] so her husband could conduct [[NASA]]-based research. She closed her workshop and intensified her scientific research into non-blown ancient glass vessels.<ref name=":1" /> 
[[File:Hedwig-glas (cropped).jpeg|thumb|Sample Hedwig glass with eagle ([[Rijksmuseum]])]]
Based on her practical work with glass and her study of ancient and medieval glasses, Lierke presented new ideas for the manufacture of glasses, especially [[cameo glass]], the [[cage cup]] and the medieval [[Hedwig glass]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Lierke |first=Rosemarie |url=http://archive.org/details/diehedwigsbecher0000lier |title=Die Hedwigsbecher : das normannisch-sizilische Erbe der staufischen Kaiser |date=2005 |publisher=Ruhpolding [Germany] : F.P. Rutzen |others=Internet Archive |isbn=978-3-938646-04-5}}</ref> Her work proved to be hotly debated and controversial in the scientific community.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hoffmann |first=Birgitta |date=2004 |title=R. Lierke's theories on ancient glass-making - ROSEMARIE LIERKE, ANTIKE GLASTÖPFEREI. EIN VERGESSENES KAPITEL DER GLASGESCHICHTE (Zaberns Bildbände zur Archäologie, Mainz 1999). Pp. 156, figs. 346. ISBN 3-8053-2442-1. |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-roman-archaeology/article/abs/r-lierkes-theories-on-ancient-glassmaking-rosemarie-lierke-antike-glastopferei-ein-vergessenes-kapitel-der-glasgeschichte-zaberns-bildbande-zur-archaologie-mainz-1999-pp-156-figs-346-isbn-3805324421/F7698DB03D25C15F0B4AF8298AC8E7F6 |journal=Journal of Roman Archaeology |language=en |volume=17 |pages=621–630 |doi=10.1017/S104775940000859X |issn=1047-7594|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

To mark Lierke's 90th birthday, an exhibition of her works took place at the [[Bad Driburg]] Glass Museum from January to August 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Macke |first=Friedhelm |title=Sonderausstellung "Rosemarie Lierke" endet am 10. August 2025 |url=https://glasmuseum-bad-driburg.de/sonderausstellung-rosemarie-lierke-endet-am-10-august-2025/ |access-date=2025-10-28 |language=de}}</ref>

== Works in museums ==
* Cylinder vase with enamel decoration (1979), Düsseldorf, [[Museum Kunstpalast]] Inv. P 1979-5 
* Vase, Düsseldorf, Museum Kunstpalast Inv. Gl 2006-208 
* Vase Maigelein, Düsseldorf, Museum Kunstpalast Inv. Gl 2006-209 
* Vase (1979), [[Toledo Museum of Art]] Inv. 1980.1014 

== Selected publications ==
* ''Ancient Glass Pottery. A Forgotten Chapter in Glass History.'' With contributions by Matthias R. Lindig, Albrecht Locher, Hans Mommsen, Beat Rütti, Barbara Schlick-Nolte, Erika Simon, Cornelius Steckner, Eva Marianne Stern, and Carina Weiß. Philipp von Zabern, Mainz 1999, ISBN 3-8053-2442-1 
* ''The Hedwig Beakers. The Norman-Sicilian Legacy of the Hohenstaufen Emperors.'' With a contribution by Rudolf Distelberger. Verlag Franz Philipp Rutzen, Ruhpolding/Mainz 2005, ISBN 3-938646-04-7<ref name=":0" /> 
* ''Non-blown ancient glass vessels – their production from the beginnings to the luxury glasses of the Romans.'' German Glass Technology Society, Offenbach, Main 2009, ISBN 978-3-921089-48-4
